methodology: The decomposition process involved analyzing both the original research topic and the generated technical specification to extract independent and self-contained atomic units. Each unit was evaluated for technical specificity and unambiguity, ensuring that they could be implemented as single requirements. The original research topic was broken down into its core components, focusing on the functionality of the shift register, the behavior of the reset signal, and the input/output specifications. The generated specification was similarly analyzed, extracting detailed descriptions of the module's behavior, timing logic, and interconnections between components.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Implement a shift register with four D flip-flops.
The module has a clock input (clk).
The module has an active-low reset input (resetn).
The module has a serial data input (in).
The module has a serial data output (out).
Data is captured on the rising edge of the clock.
Data is shifted through the four D flip-flops.
The reset signal is applied synchronously with the clock signal.
spec_atomic_units: The module implements a 4-bit serial-in serial-out (SISO) shift register.
The module has four ports: clk, resetn, in, and out.
The reset signal resetn must be high for normal operation.
On the rising edge of clk, if resetn is low, the shift register resets to 0.
The input in is shifted into the register on each rising edge of clk.
The shift register consists of four D flip-flops connected in series.
The output out is assigned the value of Q4, the output of the last D flip-flop.
The design allows for a serial-in, serial-out operation.
The reset condition is checked first in the timing logic.
